findings.title: Spawned flusher processes are never killed or terminated because the isinstance check targets the wrong process class
findings.body: SpanFlusher creates workers with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process (line 53). On Linux, that returns SpawnProcess instances, which are not instances of top-level multiprocessing.Process (the default context's process class). Therefore the new guard `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` at line 254 is false for real flusher processes. In `_ensure_processes_alive`, a hung worker is not killed before `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement, so two workers can concurrently own and flush the same shards, creating duplicate or lost segments. The same predicate at line 346 also prevents `join()` from terminating spawned workers on shutdown. Use the spawn context's process class/BaseProcess, or remove the isinstance check as the previous code did.

findings.title: Negative flusher_processes silently starts no flusher workers
findings.body: The `--flusher-processes` CLI option accepts any int and no positive-value validation is performed. If `max_processes` is negative, `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` becomes negative, `process_to_shards_map` and the process/backpressure/healthy dictionaries are all empty, and no flusher processes are created. Backpressure and memory checks then iterate over empty dictionaries, so `submit` never raises and the consumer keeps committing while spans are never flushed. Validate that `flusher_processes` is at least 1 (for example with click.IntRange(min=1)) before constructing SpanFlusher.
